results.title: Germany: Berlin student protest targets rearmament and compulsory service
results.content: Thousands of students marched through Berlin, on Friday 20 November 2026, protesting against the country's rapid military rearmament and fears of a return to compulsory military service. Their protest formed part of a wider wave of youth demonstrations across Europe.

results.title: Video shows dramatic helicopter rescue of woman trapped in flood channel
results.content: Los Angeles County firefighters rescued a woman trapped in a fast-moving flood control channel using a helicopter and an airborne paramedic.

results.title: Germany intensifies engagement with South Caucasus as 'region of opportunities'
results.content: Germany's foreign minister visited Azerbaijan and Armenia to develop projects of “strategic importance to Europe both economically and politically," in the context of Russia's aggression against Ukraine and the economic situation in Europe.

results.title: Trump defends Putin ties and accuses Iran of dishonesty in negotiations
results.content: Speaking at a White House following his trip to Asia, Trump defended his ties with Xi and Putin, claiming the Russian leader wanted to end the war in Ukraine through diplomacy. He also called for a "real deal" with Iran.

results.title: Morocco commits €366 million to build a national defence industry by 2035
results.content: The royal cabinet said the plan aims to meet 40% of the armed forces’ and security services’ equipment needs through domestic production by 2035 and to generate more than 65% of industry revenues from exports, supported by a new strategic agency, a holding company, and two new industrial zones.

results.title: Deepening EU–Canada ties: From critical minerals and defence to erasmus+
results.content: ‘We are determined to drive the renewed political momentum between the EU and Canada forward,’ write four Members of the European People’s Party (EPP) Group in the European Parliament in an op-ed for Euronews, published on the occasion of a visit by an EPP delegation to Canada on 19–21 November.

results.title: Turkey: Activists chant 'shame' as COP31 negotiations falter
results.content: Climate activists denounced the proposed outcome of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday 20 November 2026, accusing governments of failing to deliver meaningful progress on tackling climate change. They chanted "shame" as negotiations approached their deadline.

results.title: Italy: Workers and students stage nationwide strike over living costs
results.content: Workers and students marched through Rome, on Friday 20 November 2026, joining a nationwide strike over stagnant wages, rising living costs and government spending priorities. Protesters also demanded more funding for education and criticised military spending.

results.title: UAE's Lana Nusseibeh pledges ‘relentless diplomacy’ in bid to lead the UN
results.content: Lana Nusseibeh, the Emirati star diplomat running to succeed António Guterres, told Euronews the UN must return to its core purpose of peace, development, and prosperity. She has pledged relentless diplomacy, a leaner UN judged on results, and early action on wars from Ukraine to Gaza if chosen.

results.title: Ukraine: Rescue teams search wreckage after deadly Russian strike on Kyiv
results.content: A Russian overnight attack on Kyiv, Ukraine, killed eight people on Friday 20 November 2026, according to Associated Press, leaving buildings and warehouses damaged across the capital. Firefighters battled blazes as emergency crews searched the wreckage and police collected evidence.

results.title: NYC mayor unveils plan to close notorious Rikers Island jail by 2032
results.content: Rikers had been slated to close by August 2027 following legislation passed by the City Council in 2019. Moving the deadline will require a change to this law.

results.title: Estonia to shut border with Russia over GRU-linked sabotage attack
results.content: The five checkpoints will close from 1 December, with a possible review in six months, after an attempted arson at a defence facility near Tallinn that Estonian authorities say Russian military intelligence ordered. Rail services will remain unaffected.

results.title: Himalaya-sized ancient 'supermountains' found beneath Antarctica's ice sheet
results.content: The discovery offers a window into the continent's geological past and of how life on Earth has evolved.

results.title: UK anthem returns to the EU stage in symbolic post-Brexit moment
results.content: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was welcomed by EU leaders in Brussels for a summit aimed at strengthening post-Brexit relations. God Save the King rang out for the first time since Brexit at the UK–EU summit.

results.title: Vatican: Giant Christmas tree lifted into place beside St Peter's Basilica
results.content: A towering 25-metre Christmas tree was lifted into place in St Peter's Square, Vatican City, on Friday 20 November 2026, as preparations began for this year's Christmas celebrations. The silver fir, donated by a community in southern Italy, will be unveiled on 7 December.

results.title: Moving my religion: Vatican Museums explore a century of Popemobiles
results.content: From Pius XI's Mercedes to John Paul II's Popemobile: eight historic cars show how Popes' vehicles have changed. The Vatican Museums exhibition retraces a century of history, between technology, curiosities and safety.

results.title: Bhutan: Traditional wood painting shapes the kingdom's architecture
results.content: In Bhutan, artisans hand-paint intricate patterns on wooden buildings, preserving a centuries-old tradition. Known as Shing Tshon, the craft remains central to the kingdom's cultural identity.

results.title: Iran readies tanker convoy at Kharg Island to test US oil blockade
results.content: More than 14 tankers have been assigned crews and Iranian flags at the terminal that handles up to 90% of the country’s crude exports, according to satellite imagery and ship-tracking data, with a convoy expected to head toward the Sea of Oman in the coming days.

results.title: Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a visitor's hat
results.content: Fiona, the Cincinnati Zoo's much-loved hippopotamus, has died after swallowing a knitted hat that became stuck in her digestive system. Vets made several attempts to remove the object but were unable to save the nine-year-old animal.

results.title: Video shows isolated Awá Indigenous people make contact with government team in Brazil
results.content: Around 20 members of Brazil’s isolated Awá Indigenous group have approached a government outpost in the Amazon, asking for yams before returning to the forest. The rare encounter has raised concerns about their health and possible food shortages.

results.title: US: Protesters demand human control over AI after Anthropic's IPO
results.content: Protesters gathered outside Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters on 19 November 2026 to demand tighter regulation and greater human control over artificial intelligence, following the company’s $2 trillion stock market debut.

results.title: Japan: The dark secret behind an island paradise full of rabbits
results.content: Hundreds of rabbits roam freely on Japan's Okunoshima Island, delighting visitors from around the world. But behind its idyllic scenery lies a troubling history of secret chemical weapons production.

results.title: Ukraine: Kyiv metro stations become overnight shelters amid air raids
results.content: Residents of Kyiv, Ukraine, sought refuge in underground metro stations overnight on Thursday 19 November 2026, as repeated air raid alerts warned of further Russian attacks on the capital. Strikes on the Ukrainian capital killed at least one person, injured five and damaged two embassies.

results.title: 217-day underwater patrol of UK's nuclear submarine HMS Vengeance worries experts
results.content: The Royal Navy's HMS Vengeance nuclear submarine has set a new record by completing a 217-day mission. For about seven months, the crew had almost no contact with the outside world.

results.title: White House national cyber director fired after wave of tech outages
results.content: The national cyber director is tasked with advising the president on cybersecurity policy and strategy, including information security and data protection as well as deterrence of "malicious" activity.

results.content: The Trump administration pressed ahead with the auction despite a federal judge’s finding that regulators broke wildlife protection law and conservation groups vowed to have the leases voided.

results.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes damage Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv
results.content: Russian strikes damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv on Thursday. Windows were shattered and vehicles damaged, but diplomatic staff escaped unharmed.
